clue.text: Two women getting a sort of coat

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name
Mel is a woman's name, short for Melanie

explanation.surface: A pair of women acquire some kind of coat, perhaps a new jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy layer applied to metal or teeth, so it is a kind of coating.

clue.text: Joint action when someone else is being lazy?

definitions.text: Joint action when someone else is being lazy?

parts.words: Joint action when someone else is being lazy?
parts.note: the joint is the elbow, and its action is a dig in the ribs to rouse an idle companion

explanation.surface: Reads like a complaint about a shared project where one partner shirks their share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint action' suggests teamwork; here the joint is an elbow giving a lazy person a poke.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle push with the elbow is the classic way to prod someone into activity.

clue.text: Mummy with inscribed gold fish in burial chamber

indicators.note: having something inscribed means having it written inside, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: mum is a word for mummy, one's mother
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: An Egyptian mummy adorned with a golden fish lies in a tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mummy' suggests the Egyptian kind, but it is a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A mausoleum is a grand building housing a tomb, a stately burial vault.

clue.text: Go wild in first half of communication, final message

indicators.note: the first half of the six-letter word for a communication is its opening three letters

parts.note: a letter is a written communication
RIP, rest in peace, is the last message on a gravestone

explanation.surface: Someone loses control after reading the opening of a farewell note.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an idiom meaning to act without restraint.

clue.text: Water container outside prison somewhere in Somerset

parts.note: bird, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time, means a prison sentence
Bath is a city in Somerset, a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a reservoir beyond the walls of a West Country jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like a container signal but belongs to the definition: the item stands in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird bath is a basin of water put out in a garden for birds to drink and wash in.

clue.text: Idle enjoyment — maybe involving lots of falling over and rolling around in pub?

definitions.meaning: the phrase 'life is not all ...' uses it for easy pleasure

definitions.text: maybe involving lots of falling over and rolling around in pub?
definitions.meaning: skittles is a pub game where pins fall over and balls roll, alongside drinking that may make people fall over

explanation.surface: Describes a riotous night at the local with drunken people tumbling about.
explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is a traditional British pub game like bowling, knocking down nine pins with a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names carefree pleasure and amusement, as in 'life isn't all fun and games'.

clue.text: Reasonable allowance going on a learner

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance
L is the learner plate on British cars

explanation.surface: A sensible quota being given to a student driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something sensible and governed by logic.

clue.text: Father, say, in risky venture

indicators.note: one word's letters are placed in the other's

parts.note: a bet is a gamble, a risky venture
eg, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A dad, perhaps, involved in a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' is a verb here, meaning to sire.
explanation.definitionFit: To father a child is to sire or procreate, the archaic biblical verb.

clue.text: Greet a new, properly disciplined youngster

indicators.note: disciplining the letters puts them into a new, correct order

explanation.surface: An instruction to welcome a newcomer, a well-behaved child.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweenager is a child of about ten to twelve, between childhood and the teens.

clue.text: Notice honest chaps needing time to bring change

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement or notice
just means fair and honest
men are chaps

explanation.surface: An announcement saying trustworthy fellows need a while to effect reform.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjustment is a small alteration or modification.

clue.text: Dull PM of yesteryear

explanation.surface: A boring former prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey day is a dull one; Charles, 2nd Earl Grey, led the government that passed the 1832 Reform Act.

clue.text: Limes on a nutty sort of pudding

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Citrus fruit placed on a dessert flavoured with nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nutty' looks like a flavour of the pudding but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is coarse wheat grain cooked with milk into a school-dinner style dessert.

clue.text: Opposites meeting before good trip

parts.note: out is one of a pair of opposites
in is the opposite of out

explanation.surface: Contrasting people meet up before a pleasant journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is an excursion or short pleasure trip.

clue.text: What may be put in post to keep female secure

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.words: What may be put in post
parts.note: an SAE, stamped addressed envelope, is enclosed and sent by post

explanation.surface: Something posted to protect a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe means protected from harm, free of danger.

clue.text: Goddess undone by a hot pride

indicators.note: something undone has been taken apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A deity brought low by passionate vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love.

clue.text: Daughter, distinguished artist, has success penning good sketches

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a distinguished British artist

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: wins are successes

explanation.surface: A daughter who is a celebrated painter achieves acclaim with fine pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawings and sketches are both pictures made with pencil or pen.

clue.text: This person's quiet death about to happen

parts.note: the speaker saying 'this person is' gives I'm
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
an ending, the end of life

explanation.surface: Someone senses their own peaceful demise is near.
explanation.definitionFit: Impending describes something imminent, looming.

clue.text: Any number of riders, unled invaders

parts.note: n stands for an unspecified number in maths

indicators.note: without its lead, its first letter is dropped

parts.note: horsemen are riders

explanation.surface: Countless leaderless cavalry mounting an invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen were the Viking raiders who invaded Britain.

clue.text: Plant gives sheep terrible surprise according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a shock is a nasty surprise

explanation.surface: A plant frightens a sheep badly.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock is a clover-like plant, the emblem of Ireland.

clue.text: Saucy bits for suppertime

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the word are taken, a run from its middle

explanation.surface: Cheeky snacks served at the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pert means cheeky or impudent, the same sense as saucy.

clue.text: Fastener sank, ultimately blocking drain

indicators.note: a letter blocking a pipe sits inside it

parts.note: a sewer is a drain

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A clip went down and got stuck in the plughole.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a pin used to fasten meat together while cooking.

clue.text: Report of Soviet satellite's ordered system

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: Kosmos was the name of a long series of Soviet satellites

explanation.surface: News of a Russian spacecraft's organised network.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos is the universe seen as an orderly, harmonious whole.

clue.text: Car beginning to turn into desolate area

indicators.note: one letter goes into the other word

parts.note: a moor is a bleak expanse of open upland

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A car starting to swing on to bleak ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor is an informal British word for a car.

clue.text: Closely observe what till operator may do

definitions.meaning: a cashier accepts banknotes from customers

explanation.surface: A supermarket cashier watching carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay attention is the idiom; a till operator literally receives a banknote.

clue.text: Play round when king enters city

indicators.note: one piece enters another, going inside it

parts.note: to toy is to play
K is the chess abbreviation for king
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A game starts when a monarch arrives in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan.

clue.text: Glamour brings uncomfortable feeling, by the sound of it

indicators.note: tells us the word is taken as heard, not spelt

parts.note: guilt is an uncomfortable feeling of having done wrong

explanation.surface: Glitz brings a pang of remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilt means a superficial glitter or glamour, as in 'the gilt is off the gingerbread'.

clue.text: What's milky, mixed up in drink?

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: all its letters, the S included, go into the mix

explanation.surface: A question about what milky thing is stirred into a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt whisky is a spirit made from malted barley, a drink.

clue.text: The girl's items of jewellery? They come from a 'catch'

parts.note: her means belonging to the girl
rings are items of jewellery

explanation.surface: A woman's rings were won from a marriageable 'catch'.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'catch' looks like an eligible partner giving rings; it is a fishing haul.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish such as these are landed in a fishing catch.

clue.text: Country to the west in which to discover old tract

indicators.note: the other piece is found inside it
in an across clue going west means reading right to left

parts.note: Niger is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Explorers head west to find an ancient stretch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the west' turns NIGER into REGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is an area or tract of land.
